subject: Follow-up: Context length & pricing profile for Acme assistant
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>, Tom Miller <tmiller@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: context length & token-volume profile (Acme)

Hi Sarah / Tom 

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the proposed next steps so we have alignment before I put together the pricing worksheet.

Key points we captured on the call:
- Primary product: Acme virtual assistant for customers + internal doc summarization.
- Expected active users: ~500k MAU (product team estimate).
- Typical session: ~5 turns average; a subset of flows produce long outputs (documents, transcripts).
- Token profile (high level):
  - Avg prompt tokens: ~300 (range 200	6450)
  - Avg completion tokens: ~1,000 (range 200	641800)
  - Completion:prompt ratio roughly 3	64x for the heavy flows
- Monthly token volume (banded estimate): 800M 	 1.5B tokens/month (depending on adoption).
- Context-length distribution breakdown (approx):
  - 70% of requests fit within 8k context
  - 20% require 32k context (document-aware summarization/search)
  - 10% require >32k (128k) for long transcripts/batch summarization
- Budget guidance you gave on the call: target unit economics goal ~ $700	6800 per 1M tokens (committed pricing target).

Open questions I flagged for the pricing worksheet:
1) Exact monthly committed token target (helps pick Dedicated vs Hosted pricing).
2) Percent of calls that are streaming vs batch (affects latency SLO & kernel selection).
3) Any security/compliance needs that would require Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) beyond normal SOC2 controls?

Next steps:
- I will attach a pricing estimate snapshot and a token-volume scenario workbook (acme_pricing_profile.xlsx).
- If the "target $/1M" is real for procurement, we should schedule a quick internal pricing review w/ Jordan and the solutions team to scope Reserved capacity options.

Thanks  Ill follow up with the spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.


Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachment: acme_pricing_profile.xlsx (pricing scenarios workbook)

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Tom Miller <tmiller@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: context length & token-volume profile (Acme)

Marissa 

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so the worksheet can be tuned:
- The MAU estimate is our stretch target; we plan a staged rollout. Initial steady-state for year 1 we expect ~300k MAU, ramping to 500k by Q4.
- Token breakdown from our telemetry (rough):
  - Avg prompt tokens: 400 (higher for multi-document prompts)
  - Avg completion tokens: 900 (most assistant responses short, a subset long)
  - We have nightly batch jobs that generate long summaries (~128k context) for some enterprise customers  roughly 8	610% of total tokens but concentrated in a few accounts.
- Context needs: 15% of interactive requests will need 32k; the 128k usage is primarily batch summarization (not latency-sensitive).
- Procurement guidance: our CFO is targeting an operational budget that equates to ~$750 per 1M tokens if we can commit to a 12	118 month contract.

Two asks for the estimate:
1) Provide a committed pricing scenario (1M / 5M / 10M tokens/month) showing Hosted vs Dedicated (reserved) economics and the assumptions for batching / caching savings.
2) Show delta for 8k vs 32k vs 128k context; we want a clear per-1M effective price for each class (so we can model cost for the long	6tail).

Ive attached an internal procurement note that lists our target timelines.


Sarah Jones
Dir. Product, Conversational AI  Acme Corp
sarah.jones@acme.com

> Attachment: procurement_timeline.pdf (internal)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>, Tom Miller <tmiller@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: context length & token-volume profile (Acme)

Sarah  thanks for the details, very helpful. I pulled together the initial pricing scenarios and assumptions (attached: redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf). Key points / assumptions up front:

Summary of assumptions used in the worksheet:
- Baseline model = open 8k context family for 70% of traffic. Heavy-document flows use optimized 32k models; batch jobs use a 128k variant.
- Baseline hosted list price (no commit) for comparable open models: $1,200 per 1M tokens (this reflects current hosted cost for long-context-capable variants).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) economics: with a 12	118 month commit we can reach $500	700 per 1M tokens depending on committed volume and instance sizing.
- Additional unit-savings modeled:
  - KV/prefix caching + request-level batching = ~20	335% effective token cost reduction on real traffic (varies by session length and re-use).
  - Quantization and kernel optimizations on dedicated infra can add another ~10	115% savings for the same perf profile.

Example scenario (monthly tokens = 1.2B):
- Hosted (no commit): nominal ~$1,200 / 1M -> monthly cost ~ $1.44M
- Dedicated reserved (1.2B/month commit), modeled blended price: $650 / 1M -> monthly cost ~ $780k
- With caching + batching improvements (30% effective): blended $455 / 1M -> monthly cost ~ $546k

Context-class deltas (effective per-1M priced tokens):
- 8k context (baseline): base price X (as above)
- 32k context: ~1.25x baseline due to larger KV/cache working set and memory footprint on instance sizing
- 128k context (batch transcription/summarization): ~1.6	2.0x baseline for batch jobs when using specialized kernels and off-peak scheduling; note  because these are non-latency-critical we recommend scheduling on batch pools for lower unit cost.

Pricing note about your $750 target:
- $750 / 1M tokens is achievable in the Dedicated committed lane for the blended workload if you commit to ~1B+ tokens/month and accept a mix of batch scheduling for 128k jobs. The worksheet attached includes 3 committed tiers (500M, 1B, 1.5B) and shows the blended per-1M with/without caching.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal pricing review: Jordan (cc) and I will put together a short commitment vs. unit-economics memo for procurement.
- I'll add a per-context-line item table in the workbook (8k / 32k / 128k) with explicit multipliers and assumptions.
- Schedule follow-up call w/ procurement and solutions engineering to sign off on sizing and SLA.

If that looks good I can send a formal commercial summary and term sheet for your procurement team early next week.

Thanks  let me know if you want the commit scenarios adjusted (e.g., 24-month).


Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate.pdf

2) For the 128k batch jobs: confirm we can schedule them off-peak and whether you can provide a separate SKU / discounted rate for batch pools.

If we can hit $700 committed with the schedule-for-batch stipulation, we can fast-track legal and finance. Can we set a 30-minute procurement call this week?
